provenance.author: block B1 writer (Claude Opus 5.5, model-written)
notes: Beat realised in four sections: the listening lesson (Saf yma! / Gwranda!), Cai's mockery and fall into the straw man, Modlen's commands, Dafi's pie and the chase (Cer mas!). Ends on Myrddin's 'Gwers dda'.

Primary target G07: about 40 ti-imperatives (dere, cer, gwranda, saf, aros, edrych, dal, rho, cymer, paid â / ag). Contrasts with earlier forms: Dere yma. → Mae Arth yn dod.; Paid â siarad! ↔ Dw i ddim yn siarad!; Rho wellt! (SM) ↔ Rho'r bwced! / Dal y bwced! (no SM after 'r).

Continuity: Modlen sees only 'rhywbeth bach coch' ('Cath goch?') and chases Pero, so her discovery of Dafi stays in Pennod 11. Myrddin's deadpan 'Ffwrn fach yw Dafi' plants Dafi's oven job (Pennod 11).
Running words about 870 against 800 (window 720–880): the target needs dialogue (Modlen's commands), and the four sections each carry an event; nothing is restated.

Imperative forms gwranda, saf, cymer, rho and the form ag are added in lexicon-deltas/pennod-07.json so the checker licenses them; 'dewch' is the plan's declared incidental (glossed); 'ATISHŴ' is glossed in its segment as in Penodau 4–6.
Family-word recycling per the pilot note: gwraig, cogyddes, mab, chwaer, plant, menyw; tref, pell, agos (Arth: 'mae'r afon yn bell!' ↔ Modlen: 'Mae'r afon yn agos. Cer!').

Applied gpt-6-astra review (2026-10-12): pies now 'wrth ffenest y gegin' / 'wrth y ffenest' instead of 'ar y ffenest'; yn sydyn gloss no longer equates it with 'nawr (cyflym)'; Gramadeg, nodyn and pattern card now say the article blocks the imperative-object mutation while a feminine singular noun still softens after y (Cymer y bastai); un + feminine singular, ll-/rh- excepted; Pensa B b1/b2 and A a10, C c6 accept further correct answers; C c4 now fixes the moment (Modlen picking up the bucket).

Checker warnings left: local-density at s069–s078, where Modlen's burst of commands repeats the chapter's own new forms (paid, â, cer, dere, prysur, sydyn); no opaque word is first met there. lemma-validation for dere, cer, mas and deilen: already listed in chapters.json validation.not_in_corcencc for fluent sign-off.

Audit-fix pass 2026-10-19 (docs/reviews/welsh-russian-lessons-2026-10-19.md): s072 gloss 'dewch = dere + dere' read as 'come come'; now 'dewch = dere, i'r plant'. Pensa: C c1 'Ble mae'r wers?' → 'Yn y buarth' was not stated in this chapter's text; it now asks 'Sut mae Arth yn sefyll yn y wers?' → 'Ar un goes' (s016, s025); A a9/a10 accept the short answers (Nac ydw / Nac ydy) beside the full ones; C c4 accepts 'Does dim dŵr yn y bwced'.

rows: Rho wellt! ← gwellt · Cymer bastai! ← pastai

grammar.nodyn_en: To tell one friend (ti) to do something, use the command form: often the verb-noun (edrych, aros, dal), sometimes a short form (gwranda, saf, cymer, rho); dere and cer are special. 'Don't' is Paid â …, ag before a vowel. A direct object straight after a command softens (Rho wellt!), but not after 'r (Rho'r bwced!).
